groundhog-removal.extendedBody:
Upson Piedmont Red-Clay Burrow Damage

Groundhogs excavate multi-chamber burrow systems — main entrance plus 2-5 secondary openings, total tunnel length 20-50+ feet, depth 2-5 feet underground. Upson County's Piedmont red-clay soils produce slower tunneling rates than Coastal Plain sandy soils, but the eventual burrow system is equally damaging when established under structural footings. Most Upson groundhog work involves burrows under decks, sheds, barns, antebellum porches, and crawlspaces.

Thomaston pre-1900 historic-district properties are particularly vulnerable to burrow damage because antebellum porches and brick-pier crawl-space foundations are structurally older and can collapse from undermining. Thomaston Mills mill-village housing porches (1900s-1940s construction) show similar but less-developed vulnerability.

Trap-and-Relocate Plus L-Trench Exclusion

Upson groundhog work is trap-and-relocate followed by burrow-system sealing and entry-point exclusion. Upson groundhog trap placement targets the main burrow entrance with secondary-entrance monitoring across the Piedmont red-clay burrow system — particularly under Thomaston antebellum porches and Thomaston Mills mill-village structures. Georgia DNR Region 1 (Northeast) licensing applies for relocation.

Exclusion: backfill the main entrance and visible secondary entrances with compacted soil + cobble, install 1/4-inch hardware cloth around deck-skirting, shed-corner, antebellum-porch, and barn-corner perimeters dug 12-18 inches below grade and extending 12 inches outward (the L-trench that defeats re-burrowing), monitor for re-establishment over the next 4-6 weeks. Thomaston historic-district L-trench work coordinates with any pre-1900 historic-property restrictions.

faqs.q: Is antebellum Thomaston porch damage from groundhogs really structural?

faqs.q: Are groundhogs the same as woodchucks?

mole-removal.extendedBody:
Upson Piedmont Red-Clay Mole Tunneling

Eastern moles spend essentially their entire lives underground excavating two layers of tunnel: deep permanent tunnels (8-20 inches below grade) for travel and denning, and shallow feeding tunnels (1-4 inches below grade) for hunting earthworms and grubs. Across Upson County lawns — Thomaston historic-district, mill-village, and rural-acreage — the shallow feeding tunnels are what produce the visible raised lawn ridges driving most Upson residential mole calls.

Upson County's Piedmont red-clay soils slow mole tunneling rates compared to Coastal Plain sandy soils. An Upson mole typically extends tunnel systems 5-10 feet per day during peak feeding season (vs 10-20 feet per day in sandy Coastal Plain lawns). The damage still develops within 2-4 weeks of new mole arrival.

Trap-and-Remove Plus Grub-Population Management

Upson mole work centers on trap-and-remove using surface-tunnel trap placement (scissor-jaw or harpoon-style traps positioned on active shallow tunnels). On Upson lawns, identifying active vs inactive mole tunnels matters because the Piedmont red-clay structure retains exploratory-run tunnels longer than sandy soils — most visible Upson tunnels are one-time runs the mole never uses again. On an Upson lawn, mark several mole tunnels with sand or flagging, flatten them with foot pressure, check 24-48 hours for which tunnels re-raise; those are the productive trap-placement sites on Piedmont red-clay turf.

Upson mole secondary work: grub-population management on the lawn — milky spore or beneficial nematodes timed to the Piedmont seasonal window — reduces the prey base that supports mole density across Thomaston residential and rural-acreage lawns. Without grub management, even successful trapping invites re-colonization from neighboring Upson lawns. All Upson County commercial mole trapping requires Georgia DNR Region 1 (Northeast) licensing — covering Thomaston residential lawns and rural-acreage Yatesville-area properties.

faqs.q: Will poison or repellent solve my Upson mole problem?
faqs.a: Generally no. Mole repellents have limited efficacy and most residential mole-poison products are designed for gophers, not moles. Castor-oil-based products show short-term efficacy but moles return as soon as the treatment wears off. Trap-and-remove is the reliable approach.

faqs.q: How does Upson red-clay soil affect mole trap placement?
faqs.a: Red-clay soils retain tunnel structure better than sandy soils, which helps with active-tunnel identification — re-raised tunnels in red clay stay defined longer than in sandy soils. Trap success rates on Upson Piedmont lawns are comparable to other Piedmont counties.
